mainTopic: Whether a broken vessel's remaining use must resemble its original use (מעין מלאכה ראשונה): the clapperless bell, the metal animal shoe, and the עיר של זהב
overview: The גמרא explains why a bell that lost its clapper is still a כלי and can still be טמא. One reason, backed by רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, is that it can still ring when struck on earthenware. A second reason, quoted in the name of רבי יוחנן, is that it can be used to give a child water. The גמרא challenges this using a ברייתא about 'עמוד ונעשה מלאכתנו' and רבי יוחנן's view that this test applies even to טומאת מת. On that view, only a use like the original one, מעין מלאכה ראשונה, should count. The גמרא answers by switching the names in the bell dispute. It proves this is the right switch from a ברייתא about a metal animal shoe, where רבי יוחנן says it can become טמא because a person can still wear it as a shoe. The גמרא then gives the practical differences between the three opinions on the shoe: a dirty shoe and a heavy shoe. Finally it returns to the משנה and starts explaining the עיר של זהב, a golden ornament showing ירושלים. That explanation continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The bell still works by striking it on earthenware
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the answer to why a bell without its clapper is still טמא: it can still ring if you strike it against a piece of pottery.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is fit to be struck against a piece of earthenware.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering the question from the end of the previous עמוד: why is a bell still טמא after its clapper is removed? Answer: you can still make it ring by banging it on pottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A broken vessel normally becomes טהור because it is no longer a usable כלי. Here the bell can still do its original job of making a sound, just in a different way. So it is still a כלי, and its טומאה stays.

phrases.english: Since it is fit
to be struck upon earthenware
phrases.notes: Banging the bell on pottery produces a ringing sound, like a clapper would.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְרָאוּי לְהַקִּישׁוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי חֶרֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the question posed on the previous עמוד (why the clapperless bell remains טמא).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The bell remains a usable כלי because it can still produce sound when struck on earthenware.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A clapperless bell is still a כלי because it can still ring.

steps.title: An אמורא is quoted saying the same reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא gave this exact same reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: Since it is fit to be struck against earthenware.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that this reason is not just a guess. A known אמורא, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, said the very same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'איתמר נמי' means 'it was also said'. The גמרא uses it to show that an earlier authority stated the same explanation. Nothing new is added to the law; the reason simply gets backing.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also stated (introduces support from an אמורא)

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְרָאוּי לְהַקִּישׁוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי חֶרֶס.
phrases.english: Since it is fit to be struck upon earthenware.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 1 with an identical statement from an אמורא.
steps.raayaObject: The reason that the bell stays טמא because it can be struck on earthenware.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן gives a different reason: giving a child water
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the bell stays a כלי for another reason: you can use it as a little cup to give a child water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Since it is fit for giving a child water to sip from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן agrees the bell stays טמא, but he gives another reason. The hollow bell can serve as a small cup for a child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason does not rely on the bell's original job of making a sound. It relies on a completely different use, drinking. That difference is what the גמרא is about to attack.

keyTerms.meaning: to give to sip / to give a drink

steps.whyThisMatters: Because רבי יוחנן relies on a new, different use, the question becomes whether any use keeps a broken vessel a כלי, or only a use similar to the original one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Since it is fit to give a sip with it
water to a child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation from steps 1–2 for the same ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The clapperless bell stays a כלי because it can be used to give a child water.

steps.title: Doesn't רבי יוחנן require a use similar to the original?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: doesn't רבי יוחנן hold that a broken vessel keeps its status only if its remaining use is like its original use?
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רבי יוחנן not require a use similar to the original function?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to challenge רבי יוחנן. This line is a setup; the proof that he holds this way comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving a child water has nothing to do with ringing a bell. If רבי יוחנן holds elsewhere that only a similar use counts, his reason here does not fit. The question looks like a question, but it works as an attack.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a real question asking for information. It is a challenge: the גמרא thinks רבי יוחנן does require a similar use, and it is about to prove it.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yochanan not require
a use resembling the original function?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא בָּעֵי מֵעֵין מְלָאכָה רִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning רבי יוחנן gave in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reason that the bell stays a כלי because it can give a child water.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a remaining use counts only when it resembles the original function, then drinking (unlike ringing) should not keep the bell a כלי.

steps.title: A ברייתא: only an object made for sitting gets מדרס impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. A זב makes an object טמא by sitting on it only if the object is meant for sitting. It does not apply to a work-vessel that he happened to sit on.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: 'And every vessel on which he sits' — one might think that if he turned over a סאה measure or a תרקב measure and sat on it, it would be טמא. Therefore the verse says 'on which the זב sits': only something designated for sitting. This excludes an object about which we would say to him, 'Get up, so we can do our work with it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that sets up the principle 'עמוד ונעשה מלאכתנו'. A vessel whose real job is something other than sitting does not become טמא מדרס when a זב sits on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is the object's main function. If its owner would tell the זב 'get up, we need this for work', the object is not a seat. So it does not get seat-impurity. This principle is the foundation for the dispute in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: a man with a specific bodily discharge who transmits impurity
dry measures (a סאה and a half-סאה)
'Get up so we can do our work': the test that an object's real use is not sitting

phrases.english: But was it not taught (in a ברייתא):
'And every vessel on which he sits, etc.' (Vayikra 15:4)
One might think: if he overturned a se'ah-measure and sat on it,
or overturned a tarkav-measure and sat on it,
it would be impure;
therefore the verse says:
'on which the zav sits' —
that which is designated for sitting;
excluding this one, about which we say to him:
'Get up, and we will do our work (with it).'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that sets up the principle needed to prove the challenge in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The principle 'עמוד ונעשה מלאכתנו': an object's main function decides its status.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the principle applies only to מדרס
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the 'get up, we need it for work' test applies only to מדרס impurity, not to טומאת מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: With regard to מדרס impurity we say 'Get up and we will do our work,' but with regard to טומאת מת we do not say 'Get up and we will do our work.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a dispute about how far this principle reaches. רבי אלעזר limits it to the impurity of a זב sitting or lying (מדרס).
steps.deeperAnalysis: For טומאת מת, רבי אלעזר does not use this test. So a broken vessel that still has some other use stays a כלי, even if that use differs from its original one. On his view, a different use is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: impurity a זב or נדה transmits by sitting, lying, or leaning on an object
impurity from contact with a dead body

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
Regarding midras-impurity, we say
'Get up and we will do our work,'
but we do not say regarding corpse-impurity
'Get up and we will do our work.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a dispute on the scope of the principle from step 5. This dispute is part of the challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'עמוד ונעשה מלאכתנו' test applies only to מדרס, not to טומאת מת.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the principle applies even to טומאת מת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the 'get up, we need it for work' test applies even to טומאת מת. This seems to contradict his reason about the bell.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: We say even with regard to טומאת מת, 'Get up and we will do our work.'
steps.whatsHappening: This completes the challenge. רבי יוחנן himself holds that an object's original function decides its status even for טומאת מת, so a different use should not keep a broken vessel a כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the original function is what counts, a bell that can no longer ring should be considered broken and טהור. Being usable as a child's cup should not matter. That contradicts רבי יוחנן's reason in step 3. The answer comes next.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן said the bell stays a כלי because it can give a child water. Yet he also holds that 'עמוד ונעשה מלאכתנו' applies even to טומאת מת, meaning only the original function counts. The גמרא must resolve this contradiction.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the central question of the סוגיא: does a broken כלי stay a כלי because of any remaining use, or only because of a use like its original one?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
One says even regarding corpse-impurity
'Get up and we will do our work.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אַף אוֹמֵר בִּטְמֵא מֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוחנן's side of the dispute, which completes the challenge raised in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן requires a use resembling the original function (מעין מלאכה ראשונה).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's own statement extending 'עמוד ונעשה מלאכתנו' to טומאת מת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even for טומאת מת only the main function counts, giving a child water cannot keep a bell, whose function is ringing, a כלי.

steps.title: Switch the names in the first dispute
steps.stepSummary: To remove the contradiction, the גמרא switches the names in the bell dispute. The 'cup for a child' reason was not said by רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 7. It says that in the bell dispute, the names of the two אמוראים should be switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the switch, רבי יוחנן never said the bell stays a כלי because a child can drink from it. That reason belongs to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. So רבי יוחנן's other view stands: a new use only counts if it matches the original use, and the 'get up, we need it for work' test applies even to טומאת מת. Now his two statements no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse / switch (the names of who said what)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not changing anyone's opinion here. It is only fixing which אמורא said which opinion.

phrases.english: Reverse the first one.
phrases.notes: Switch the names in the bell dispute.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן said the bell stays a כלי because it can be used as a child's cup.
steps.terutzMaskana: That reason belongs to the other אמורא, so רבי יוחנן stays consistent.

steps.title: Why switch the first dispute and not the second?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why it chose to switch the bell dispute. It could just as easily have switched the names in the dispute with רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see that made you reverse the first one? Reverse the latter one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer. Either dispute could have been switched to fix the contradiction, so why pick the first one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we switched the second dispute instead, רבי יוחנן would be the one who limits the 'get up' test to מדרס only. Then he could keep the bell reason. Both switches remove the contradiction, so the choice needs a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? (Why choose this option over the other one?)

phrases.english: And what did you see that you reversed the first one?
Reverse the latter one!
phrases.notes: Switch רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר instead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the choice made in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The decision to switch the first dispute rather than the second
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both switches would fix the contradiction equally well, so choosing the first one seems arbitrary.

steps.title: We already know רבי יוחנן requires the same type of use
steps.stepSummary: We switch the first dispute because we know from another source that רבי יוחנן requires the new use to be like the original use.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we have heard that רבי יוחנן requires a use similar to the original work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why it switched the first dispute. Another source tells us what רבי יוחנן really holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside evidence shows that רבי יוחנן requires מֵעֵין מְלָאכָה רִאשׁוֹנָה. The bell reason (a child's cup) does not fit that rule, so that is the statement that must be reassigned. The next steps bring the evidence.

keyTerms.meaning: We have heard him (we know his view from elsewhere)
A use similar to the original use

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key principle that decides which version of רבי יוחנן's opinion is the true one.

phrases.english: For we have heard regarding Rabbi Yoḥanan
that he requires a use similar to the original work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Outside evidence about רבי יוחנן's established view
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the first switch fits רבי יוחנן's known requirement of מעין מלאכה ראשונה.

steps.title: A metal animal shoe can become טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: a metal shoe made for an animal can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: a metal shoe of an animal is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source it promised. A ברייתא says a metal shoe made for an animal can become טמא. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלי made only for animals normally cannot become טמא. So the ברייתא implies this shoe has some human use. The גמרא will now ask what that use is.

phrases.english: As it was taught: a shoe of an animal
made of metal is ritually impure (can become impure).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the claim in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן requires מעין מלאכה ראשונה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא about a metal animal shoe

steps.title: What human use does the animal shoe have?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a person could use this animal shoe for.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what is it fit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the three answers coming next. What can a person do with an animal's shoe?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since it can become טמא, it must have some human use. Finding that use is what will reveal רבי יוחנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: For what is it fit / usable?

phrases.english: For what is it fit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ברייתא in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What human use makes a metal animal shoe a כלי that can become טמא

steps.title: Three uses: drinking, oil, or wearing it
steps.stepSummary: רב says a person can drink water from it. רבי חנינא says a person can smear oil from it. רבי יוחנן says a person can wear it on his foot when running away from battle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: it is fit to drink water from in war. רבי חנינא said: it is fit to smear oil from in war. רבי יוחנן said: when he flees from battle, he puts it on his foot and runs over thorns and thistles.
steps.whatsHappening: Three אמוראים answer the question. רבי יוחנן's answer is the proof the גמרא needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן picks a use that is still a shoe: a person wears it. That is the same type of use as the original one. This shows he requires מעין מלאכה ראשונה, so he could not have said the bell becomes a child's cup.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן only counts a new use that matches the original use (a shoe stays a shoe). That is why the bell statement was reassigned to someone else.
steps.whyThisMatters: This proves which name switch is correct, and it settles רבי יוחנן's consistent view.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: רָאוּי לִשְׁתּוֹת בּוֹ מַיִם בַּמִּלְחָמָה.
phrases.english: Rav said: It is fit to drink water from it in war.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: רָאוּי לָסוּךְ בּוֹ שֶׁמֶן בַּמִּלְחָמָה.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Ḥanina said: It is fit to smear oil from it in war.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁבּוֹרֵחַ מִן הַקְּרָב
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: At the time when one flees from battle
he puts it on his feet
and runs over thorns and thistles.
phrases.notes: It's still being used as a shoe, the same kind of use it had to begin with.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: רָאוּי לִשְׁתּוֹת בּוֹ מַיִם בַּמִּלְחָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 and completes the proof for step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Drinking water (רב), smearing oil (רבי חנינא), wearing it on the foot (רבי יוחנן)

steps.title: What is the difference between רב and רבי חנינא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the practical difference between רב's explanation and רבי חנינא's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between רב and רבי חנינא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes a short side trip. It asks in what case רב and רבי חנינא would rule differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both explanations treat the shoe as a container, so the difference between them is not obvious. The גמרא wants a case where the result changes.

phrases.english: What is the difference between Rav and Rabbi Ḥanina?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question about the opinions in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between drinking from it and smearing oil from it

steps.title: A dirty shoe
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a disgusting, dirty shoe. Nobody would drink from it, but it could still hold oil for smearing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is when it is disgusting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two opinions differ when the shoe is repulsive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, a dirty shoe cannot become טמא, because no one would drink from it. According to רבי חנינא, it can still be used for oil, so it can become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

phrases.english: There is a difference between them where it is repulsive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A dirty shoe: not טמא according to רב, טמא according to רבי חנינא

steps.title: What is the difference between רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the practical difference between רבי יוחנן's explanation and רבי חנינא's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Between רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second side question. When would רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא rule differently?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dirty shoe can still be worn and can still hold oil, so the dirty case does not separate these two. The גמרא needs a different case.

phrases.english: Between Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Ḥanina?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same type of question as step 14, now for a different pair.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between wearing it and smearing oil from it

steps.title: A heavy shoe
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a heavy shoe. It is too heavy to wear while running, but it could still hold oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is when it is heavy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן and רבי חנינא differ when the shoe is heavy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן, a heavy shoe cannot become טמא, because no one could run in it. According to רבי חנינא, it can still hold oil, so it can become טמא.
steps.whatToRemember: Dirty shoe: רב says not טמא, רבי חנינא says טמא. Heavy shoe: רבי יוחנן says not טמא, רבי חנינא says טמא.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them where it is heavy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A heavy shoe: not טמא according to רבי יוחנן, טמא according to רבי חנינא

steps.title: Quoting the next item in the משנה: a city of gold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that a woman may not go out on שבת with an עיר של זהב, a 'city of gold'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not with a city of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a new phrase from the משנה. This step only sets things up so the גמרא can explain that phrase next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The talk about the shoe (steps 13-17) is finished, and the גמרא moves to the next ornament on the משנה's list. The משנה says a woman should not wear an עיר של זהב into the public domain on שבת. It does not say what this ornament actually is, so the גמרא will ask.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And not', which continues the משנה's list of things a woman may not go out with
'A city of gold', the name of a type of golden ornament

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new rule made up by the גמרא. It is a quote of words that already appear in the משנה, brought here so they can be explained.

phrases.english: And not with a city of gold.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, which lists items a woman may not wear into the public domain on שבת.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה (it could be read as the opening half of the question in the next step)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the shoe discussion and opens a new topic by quoting the next item in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may not go out on שבת wearing an עיר של זהב.

steps.title: What is a city of gold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by the phrase עיר של זהב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'a city of gold'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question: what kind of object is this 'city of gold'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody can wear an actual city, so the name must refer to some kind of jewelry. The גמרא wants to know exactly which ornament the משנה is talking about. This is a request for information, not a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is?' The standard Aramaic way to ask for the meaning of a word or phrase
'With a city'. The בְּ־ means 'with', as in wearing it

phrases.english: What is 'with a city of gold'?
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats the משנה's words in order to ask what they mean.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the term quoted in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ornament the משנה means by עיר של זהב.

steps.title: It is a golden ירושלים ornament
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה, in the name of רבי יוחנן, explains that an עיר של זהב is a 'Jerusalem of gold', a gold ornament with the city of ירושלים pictured on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: it is a ירושלים of gold,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the 'city of gold' is a golden ornament with a picture of ירושלים on it. The sentence continues into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'city' in the name is ירושלים, and the ornament is called a city because the city is engraved or pictured on it. It is a gold piece worn on the head, like a tiara or crown. Now that we know what the item is, the משנה's rule against wearing it outside on שבת is about a real piece of jewelry.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Jerusalem of gold', a gold ornament showing the city of ירושלים
Gold (Aramaic, the same word as Hebrew זָהָב)

steps.whatToRemember: An עיר של זהב is a 'ירושלים of gold', a golden head ornament with the city of ירושלים pictured on it.
steps.confusionAlert: 'ירושלים' here is not the city itself. It is the picture shown on the piece of jewelry.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
A Jerusalem of gold,
phrases.notes: A gold ornament with ירושלים pictured on it. The sentence continues on the next עמוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: יְרוּשָׁלַיִם דְּדַהֲבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An עיר של זהב is a golden ornament showing the city of ירושלים.
